title: Multi-tenant ingress fanout with opaque lease and dedicated trace hooks
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Private and Dedicated customers ingest observability (traces/metrics/logs) via perimeter collectors that sometimes cause noisy cross-tenant resource contention and trace attribution ambiguity during bursty workloads and collector cold starts. This ticket implements an ingress fanout that gives each tenant an opaque processing lease and a small, dedicated trace-hook adapter that ensures trace context is preserved without leaking tenant-identifying fields. Goals: reduce cross-tenant contention during spikes, maintain trace fidelity for debugging, preserve privacy by enforcing opaque tenant envelopes, and provide telemetry surfaces for latency/error dashboards scoped per tenant. Constraints: must be compatible with existing on-prem collector install (agent v2), operate with limited memory on edge gateways, and support tenant-level sampling and replay without adding per-request auth roundtrips.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress gateway can create and manage opaque leases per tenant id with TTL and backpressure signals
Trace-hook adapter attaches a tenant-scoped opaque envelope id to spans and preserves parent-child relationships across collectors without adding PII into span attributes
Under a simulated burst (10x baseline for 5 minutes), tenant-level queueing prevents 1 noisy tenant from increasing end-to-end 95th percentile latency for other tenants by more than 10%
Per-tenant dashboards expose: ingest latency histogram, collector queue depth, drop rate, and error rate; dashboards wired to console release console-2026.03
E2E test coverage: unit tests for envelope encoding/decoding, integration test with sidecar simulating cold starts, and load test results committed to the ticket
Docs updated: onprem collector upgrade notes, config knobs for lease TTL, sampling, and tenant-level retention policies
comments: 2026-02-18 Ava Chen: Initial writeup and proposed design attached. Marking P1 since customers have reported noisy-tenant incidents in last two weeks.
2026-02-22 Liam O'Connor: Spike completed. Implemented proof-of-concept lease table in the ingress gateway. Observed 60% reduction in cross-tenant queue spill when lease TTL tuned to 30s.

2026-02-27 SRE review (Priya Rao): Raised question about lease persistence across gateway restarts — prefer ephemeral short TTLs and rely on idempotent envelopes. Added follow-up to persist small lease cache in local disk for faster recovery.

2026-03-03 Design feedback (Diego Martinez): Suggested moving sampling decision into owner-side SDK to avoid repeated sampling calls at gateway. Agreed to provide hook API for owner SDKs to set tenant-sampling hint.
2026-03-05 Liam O'Connor: Opened PR for trace-hook adapter. See #2486. Needs security review for envelope format and KMS usage when running in air-gapped clusters.

2026-03-09 Security (Natasha Singh): Reviewed envelope scheme; recommended HMAC with tenant-scoped key stored in KMS and falling back to local ephemeral key when KMS unreachable. Added remediation steps for key rotation.

2026-03-10 Load test results uploaded: 10 tenants, one noisy tenant at 20x baseline. Tenant 95th latency for others stayed within 8% delta. Attached JMeter results to artifacts folder. Next: harden replay path and finalize dashboard panels.
implementation_notes: Ingress gateway will maintain a per-tenant token lease with metadata: opaque_envelope_id, last_seen, TTL, backpressure_counter
Envelope format: base64(HMAC(tenant_key, tenant_id || timestamp || nonce) || nonce || flags). No tenant name or email included in envelope payload
Trace-hook adapter will map original trace-id -> (envelope_id, child-span-id) and translate when forwarding to internal collectors; use consistent sampling bit handling per W3C trace context
Backpressure strategy: when tenant queue depth exceeds soft threshold, mark lease as throttled and return 429s with Retry-After or apply tail-drop depending on tenant tier
Local fallback: when KMS unreachable in private deploy, generate ephemeral tenant keys stored in secure tmpfs with rotation at 6 hours and audit log entries
Metrics emitted: tenant.ingest.queue_depth, tenant.ingest.drop_count, tenant.trace.hooks_attached, tenant.lease.expiry_seconds
Dashboard wiring: add derived alert rule 'tenant_ingest_saturation' when more than 5% tenants have queue_depth > 90th percentile for > 2m
risks: Risk: Mis-implemented envelope could leak tenant id into downstream logs. Mitigation: static analysis check on encoder, schema fuzz tests, and security review sign-off.
Risk: Lease-table growth for orgs with thousands of tenants. Mitigation: implement LRU eviction and shard leases by tenant hash; benchmark memory usage on 8GB edge VMs.
Risk: Increased complexity for on-prem upgrade. Mitigation: provide an opt-in config and a compatibility mode that uses legacy attributes until customers opt in via console flag
qa_steps: Unit test: envelope generation and validation including tamper detection
Integration: deploy ingress gateway + collector stack in a CI ephemeral cluster and run a 30-minute simulated burst test with noisy tenant; assert SLA bounds
Security: run static secret scan and ensure no tenant identifiers are present in artifacts
Manual: run through upgrade path using the onprem upgrade script and validate dashboards populate for an existing customer
Performance: memory and CPU profiling on gateway under mixed load (1000 concurrent leases)
